issues.title: Single underscore include guard used
issues.description: The rule requires header files to use include guards with double underscores at the start (e.g., __FILENAME_H), but the code uses a single underscore prefix instead (_REDIS_H)
issues.rule_name: Header Files Must Use Double-Underscore Include Guards

issues.title: Unsigned integer wraparound in AOF corruption size check
issues.description: The size comparison casts both operands to size_t (unsigned), which causes undefined behavior when valid_up_to exceeds sb.st_size. In this edge case, the subtraction sb.st_size - valid_up_to produces a negative value that wraps around to a very large unsigned integer, always exceeding aof_load_broken_max_size. This prevents automatic recovery even when the corruption is actually small, causing the server to fail to start when it should recover successfully.

issues.title: Incorrect early exit prevents loading incremental AOF after successful base recovery
issues.description: The error handling condition incorrectly treats AOF_BROKEN_RECOVERED as a failure state, causing the function to exit immediately after successfully recovering a corrupted base AOF file. When a base AOF is the last file and gets successfully recovered (ret == AOF_BROKEN_RECOVERED), the server should continue to load any incremental AOF files. However, this bug causes an early exit to cleanup, preventing incremental files from being loaded and potentially losing data. The correct behavior is to only exit on AOF_OPEN_ERR or AOF_FAILED, not on successful recovery.

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #14058 - Add auto-repair options for broken AOF tail on startup
pr.author: unknown

structured_output.summary:
The PR adds two opt-in settings, `aof-load-broken` (default `no`) and `aof-load-broken-max-size` (default 4096 bytes). When an AOF hits a format error and the bytes from the last good command to EOF are under the limit, startup truncates the file at the last good offset and continues loading. The change wires the config through `config.c` and `server.h`, adds an `AOF_BROKEN_RECOVERED` return code in `aof.c`, and adds integration tests in `tests/integration/aof.tcl`. The motivation is reducing downtime after power loss, where the AOF tail can be zero-filled or garbage.

The core idea is reasonable and the config plumbing is consistent. The problem is the recovery mechanics. `valid_up_to` is the only offset used for truncation, and it is wrong in two cases. It is never advanced after an RDB preamble is loaded, so a corrupt tail on a small RDB-base AOF truncates the whole file to 0 bytes. It also advances inside an open MULTI block, so truncating there leaves a dangling transaction that the next load reverts, discarding writes made after recovery. The truncation also happens before the code knows whether the file is the last one, so a middle-chain file is rewritten on disk and the server still exits. `DEBUG LOADAOF` does not handle the new return code. The tests have gaps: one assertion passes on either of two log lines, and the 'corrupted last file' test runs after the corruption has already been removed by an earlier start.

I would not merge this as is. The data-loss paths are reachable in the exact crash scenario the feature targets, and the fixes are local."
structured_output.verdictRationale: The feature is opt-in, so the default is safe. But the recovery path can silently discard data in two reachable scenarios: a small RDB-preamble base with a corrupt tail, and a crash mid-transaction followed by a zero-filled tail. Both need fixing before the feature is trustworthy. The truncate-then-fail behavior and the test gaps should also be addressed.

architecture.overview:
Today, AOF loading lives in `loadSingleAppendOnlyFile()` in `src/aof.c`. It is called once per file from `loadAppendOnlyFiles()`, which `loadDataFromDisk()` in `src/server.c` invokes at startup, and `DEBUG LOADAOF` in `src/debug.c` invokes at runtime. The parser reads RESP commands, runs each on a fake client, and tracks `valid_up_to`, the byte offset after the last command it executed. On a short read, the `uxeof` path can truncate the file to `valid_up_to` when `aof-load-truncated` is set. On a format error, the code jumps to `fmterr` and fails the load, and `loadDataFromDisk` calls `exit(1)`.

This PR adds a second recovery route. When `aof-load-broken` is enabled and the bytes from `valid_up_to` to EOF are under `aof-load-broken-max-size`, the `fmterr` label truncates the file at `valid_up_to`, returns `AOF_BROKEN_RECOVERED`, and continues. `valid_up_to` is now also recorded when `aof-load-broken` is on. `loadAppendOnlyFiles()` treats the new code like `AOF_TRUNCATED`: it is only accepted for the last file, and a non-last file becomes a fatal error. The settings are registered in `config.c` and stored in new `redisServer` fields in `server.h`.
steps: Entry point: `loadDataFromDisk()` in `src/server.c` calls `loadAppendOnlyFiles()`, which walks the manifest's base file and then the incr files, calling `loadSingleAppendOnlyFile()` on each.

Configuration: `aof-load-broken` (bool, default no) and `aof-load-broken-max-size` (default 4096) are registered in `src/config.c` and stored in new `redisServer` fields in `src/server.h`. A new `AOF_BROKEN_RECOVERED` return code is added.

Parser bookkeeping: `valid_up_to` is updated after each command when `aof-load-truncated` or `aof-load-broken` is on. The RDB-preamble path and the MULTI path (`valid_before_multi`) are where this offset can be wrong, as described in the findings.
Recovery branch: the `fmterr` label truncates the file to `valid_up_to` if the broken tail is small enough, then jumps to `loaded_ok`. Otherwise it logs the reason and returns `AOF_FAILED`.

Caller handling: `loadAppendOnlyFiles()` gives `AOF_BROKEN_RECOVERED` the same last-file rule as `AOF_TRUNCATED`. The value still flows to `loadDataFromDisk()` and `DEBUG LOADAOF`, which were not updated for it.

findings.title: Recovery can silently erase writes made after a crash mid-MULTI
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/aof.c`, the `fmterr` recovery branch in `loadSingleAppendOnlyFile` (around lines 1724-1746) truncates the AOF to `valid_up_to`. But `valid_up_to` is advanced after every command, including commands queued inside an open MULTI, so truncation can leave a dangling MULTI with no EXEC. Later writes then get swallowed and reverted on the next load. Before the truncate, if `fakeClient->flags & CLIENT_MULTI` is set, use `valid_before_multi` as the truncation offset, mirroring the EOF handling near line 1672. Add an integration test in `tests/integration/aof.tcl` that writes MULTI with queued commands followed by garbage, starts with `aof-load-broken yes`, then writes a new command and restarts, asserting the new command survives.

findings.title: RDB-preamble base with a corrupt tail is truncated to zero bytes
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/aof.c` `loadSingleAppendOnlyFile`, after the RDB preamble is loaded successfully (the `rdbLoadRio` success branch around lines 1541-1552), set `valid_up_to` to the current file offset (`ftello(fp)`) when `aof_load_broken` or `aof_load_truncated` is enabled. Otherwise the `fmterr` recovery can truncate the file to 0 and delete the RDB preamble. Keep the existing `valid_up_to` update in the command loop. Add an integration test in `tests/integration/aof.tcl` with an RDB-format base file, a small dataset, and a garbage tail, asserting the preamble data survives recovery.

findings.title: Truncation happens before the last-file check, so a failed startup has already rewritten the file
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/aof.c`, the `fmterr` recovery branch in `loadSingleAppendOnlyFile` (around lines 1724-1746) truncates the file before the caller knows whether it is the last file. In `loadAppendOnlyFiles` (around lines 1836 and 1870), a non-last file is turned into AOF_FAILED, and the server then exits after the file was already modified. Move the destructive truncate out of `loadSingleAppendOnlyFile`: return `AOF_BROKEN_RECOVERED` with the target offset recorded, and perform the truncate in `loadAppendOnlyFiles` only after confirming the file is the last one and the load otherwise succeeded. Keep the size-limit check where it is. Update the 'Intermediate AOF is broken' test in `tests/integration/aof.tcl` to assert the middle file is byte-for-byte unchanged after the failed startup.

findings.title: Two-pattern log assertion passes on either line, so it does not verify the fatal path
findings.body:
`wait_for_log_messages` returns as soon as any one pattern matches (`tests/support/util.tcl`, around line 213). The 'Log should mention truncated file is not last' test lists two patterns, so it passes on the 'AOF loaded anyway' line alone. That line is printed before the fatal error, so the test can pass even if the server never reaches the 'not the last file' check, or if that check is removed entirely.

::code{file="tests/integration/aof.tcl" lines="714-721"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `tests/integration/aof.tcl` around lines 714-721, the test 'Log should mention truncated file is not last' passes `wait_for_log_messages` with two patterns, but that helper returns on any single match. Split this into two `wait_for_log_messages` calls, one for '*Fatal error: the truncated file is not the last file*' and one for the 'AOF loaded anyway' message, or assert both in sequence. Check that the fatal error line is found after the recovery line.

findings.title: 'Corrupted last AOF file' test does not exercise corruption
findings.fixPrompt: In `tests/integration/aof.tcl` around lines 818-838, the 'Corrupted last AOF file: Server should still start and recover' test has no corruption left to recover. The earlier start already truncated the mid file, so the swap moves clean files around. Before the final `start_server_aof`, recreate the trailing corruption (for example by appending 'CORRUPTION') on the file that is now the last incr file, and assert that the file size drops to the valid offset after the start. Keep the `fo` == 'mid' assertion.

findings.title: DEBUG LOADAOF reports an error for a successful recovery
findings.fixPrompt: Update the success checks that now have to accept the new `AOF_BROKEN_RECOVERED` return value. In `src/debug.c` around line 600 (`DEBUG LOADAOF`), treat `AOF_BROKEN_RECOVERED` like `AOF_TRUNCATED` so a recovered load is not reported as an error. In `src/aof.c` `loadSingleAppendOnlyFile`'s cleanup (around line 1894), pass success for `AOF_BROKEN_RECOVERED` too, so module LOADING_ENDED fires instead of LOADING_FAILED. Add a test that runs DEBUG LOADAOF after a recovered load and expects +OK.

findings.title: Misleading 'AOF loaded anyway' message precedes a fatal exit
findings.body:
On the success branch, the log says 'AOF loaded anyway because aof-load-broken is enabled'. If the recovered file is not last, `loadAppendOnlyFiles` immediately logs 'Fatal error' and the server exits. Operators reading the log see both lines and cannot tell whether the load succeeded.

::diff{file="src/aof.c" lines="1736-1744"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/aof.c` in the `fmterr` recovery branch (around lines 1736-1744), the message 'AOF loaded anyway ...' is logged before the caller decides whether the file is last. Change the wording to describe the truncation itself (for example 'Truncated broken AOF tail at offset X, size Y below aof-load-broken-max-size Z'). If the truncation moves to the caller as recommended in the truncate-before-last-file finding, move the message there too.

findings.title: Dead branch: valid_up_to == -1 is unreachable in the new code
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/aof.c` `fmterr` recovery branch (around lines 1725-1727), the `valid_up_to == -1` check is unreachable because `valid_up_to` starts at 0 and is only set from `ftello`. Either remove the branch or add a comment saying why it stays. Keep the behavior consistent with the matching check in `uxeof` (around line 1694).

findings.title: redis.conf understates what the option discards
findings.body:
The new comment says Redis 'will truncate the corrupted data', but the implementation truncates everything from the first bad byte to EOF, including any valid commands after it. The size limit bounds that amount, but the comment does not say so. Operators could read the 4096-byte default as the size of the bad bytes and expect only garbage to be removed.

The comment also says the option is 'more aggressive than aof-load-truncated', which is accurate but does not say that recovery applies to any file in the chain, or that it can run on a zero-filled tail after a MULTI.

::suggestion{file="redis.conf" lines="1532-1548"}
# When the AOF contains a format error (for example garbage bytes after a
# crash), and everything from the last well-formed command to the end of the
# file is smaller than aof-load-broken-max-size, Redis truncates the file at the
# last good command and starts. Note that this removes every byte after that
# point, including any well-formed commands that happen to follow the error.
# Otherwise the server exits and needs manual repair with redis-check-aof.
# Disabled by default because truncation can lose data.
aof-load-broken no
aof-load-broken-max-size 4096
findings.fixPrompt: In `redis.conf` around lines 1532-1548, the `aof-load-broken` comment says Redis 'will truncate the corrupted data', which understates the effect. Truncation removes everything from the first bad byte to EOF, including valid commands after it. Rewrite the comment so it says the removed region is measured from the last good command to EOF, that valid commands after the error are removed too, and that the limit applies per file. Keep the default values unchanged.

findings.title: Unrelated include-guard rename in server.h
findings.body:
The diff renames the include guard from `__REDIS_H` to `_REDIS_H`. That change has nothing to do with AOF recovery. Identifiers that begin with an underscore followed by an uppercase letter are reserved for the implementation, so `_REDIS_H` is no more correct than `__REDIS_H`. It also adds noise to a header change that is otherwise about two config fields and one return code.

::diff{file="src/server.h" lines="15-16"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/server.h` lines 15-16, revert the include guard rename from `_REDIS_H` back to `__REDIS_H`. This change is unrelated to the AOF broken-tail feature, so keep the PR focused on the config fields and the `AOF_BROKEN_RECOVERED` return code.

findings.title: Config wiring and the bounded-size check are done right
findings.body:
The two options follow the existing pattern. `aof-load-broken` is a bool with default no, which fits an opt-in data-loss-risk setting. `aof-load-broken-max-size` is an `off_t` field registered through `createOffTConfig` with a lower bound of 0, so a negative value is rejected. The size comparison casts both sides to `size_t` after the bound is applied, so there is no sign issue there.

The recovery branch also guards the `lseek` on `server.aof_fd != -1`. At startup the AOF fd is not open yet, so that guard is required. The `goto loaded_ok` path restores `server.aof_state`, which the other exits in the function also depend on.
